first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ, both directly matching the documented durable wins from memory_31 and memory_86 (signup simplification and shortened onboarding lifted activation and completion without noted harm). This is the lowest-risk, highest-confidence lever available this week and addresses two of the three current problems simultaneously. Promotional pricing is tempting given competitor pressure, but memory_73 explicitly warns that SMB promotional pricing boosts short-term acquisition while materially damaging 30-day retention — a direct conflict with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I'm not choosing it this cycle. I verify memory_86 to confirm the onboarding shortening record before committing scarce experiment capacity to it, and memory_73 to double-check the retention-harm finding still holds as stated, since competitor pricing pressure creates strong pull toward that option despite the known long-term cost. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are valid but not responsive to this week's most urgent, quantified declines. Scaling as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) preserves ability to course-correct if the current onboarding change interacts differently with the new competitive pricing environment.

final.rationale: Archive confirms exp_86: shortened onboarding produced +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention — a clean, durable, positive-retention result that directly targets this quarter's documented 4% onboarding and 6% activation declines. Archive also confirms exp_73's discounting result was even worse than the summary suggested: +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue short-term, but -12% 30-day retention with explicit conclusion that the acquired cohort does not survive the first renewal cycle. That is a textbook sacrifice of long-term qualified revenue for short-term metrics, directly contrary to the stated primary objective, so promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure. Simplify_onboarding is the only candidate with verified evidence of improving both activation-adjacent metrics and retention simultaneously, making it the correct single-slot experiment this week. Running it as a standard (not broad) experiment preserves optionality to reassess given the unprecedented competitive pricing context, which none of our historical experiments were run against — so full generalization should still be treated cautiously and monitored post-launch for interaction effects with the competitor's pricing move.
